prompt: Edit the supplied sprite sheet into a corrected 12-frame seamless Sora run-loop sprite sheet. Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the original artwork and character/style reference; work directly from its smooth detailed cel-shaded KH2 Sora, outfit, hair, gloves, oversize yellow/black shoes, and Kingdom Key. Preserve that artwork finish and character identity. Output one clean landscape transparent RGBA sheet, exactly 4 columns by 3 rows, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom, 12 equal-sized cells with generous transparent gutters. Every complete figure including hair, both shoes, chain and entire Keyblade stays wholly inside its cell, no overlaps or cropping, no labels or text. Fixed right-facing three-quarter camera and fixed character scale, consistent anatomy, shoe size, clothing construction, head/hair volume and torso lean throughout. Animate in place, stable horizontal body anchor. Ground height identical in all cells; support shoe soles align on that ground while genuine flight poses are above it. Correct alternating leg roles: frames 1-6 one half-stride (far-leg contact, compression, recovery/passing of near leg, far toe-off, flight, near precontact), frames 7-12 complementary half-stride (near contact, compression, far recovery/passing, near toe-off, flight, far precontact). Show true articulated changing hip/knee/ankle poses and consistent limbs, never repeated stride drawings or scaled copies. Empty near/front arm counter-swings naturally opposite the near leg, backward when that leg reaches forward and forward when it trails; empty gloved fist must remain clear of the blade and never appear to grip it. Far/rear arm is ALWAYS the carrying arm, holding Kingdom Key over that same far shoulder behind his head. All frames retain one identical rigid Kingdom Key design: same guard, handle, shaft length, blade thickness, teeth and attached chain, connected correctly to the same carrying hand. Keep the same weapon angle relative to shoulders with only small coherent body bob; no changing blade length, detached weapon or switching hands. Small coherent body compression and flight bob, subtle cloth/chain follow-through. Last frame is immediately before the first frame's far-foot contact, making the last-to-first transition the same smooth progression as other adjacent poses; don't duplicate the first frame as the last. Correct the source's weak arm swing, repeated leg roles, changing proportions/weapon geometry and abrupt wrap while preserving source-quality rich curved anatomy, clean outlines, folds, skin/glove details and shoe shading. Actual transparent background, no painted checkerboard, matte, shadows on backdrop or scene.
